mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week improvement in WORKPLACES (-14.6 to -13.0) reflects a gradual return to commuting routines, which mechanically raises daytime foot traffic near workplaces and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as incidental shopping and lunch trips increase.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose each week from -14.6 to -13.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its monotonic weekly improvement for all four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in TRANSIT usage (-39.3 to -37.4) indicates increased willingness to travel for non-essential purposes, which directly feeds into higher retail and recreation visitation since transit access is a precondition for many retail trips in Melbourne's urban core.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -39.3 to -37.4 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days does not exceed the prior 14-day mean despite TRANSIT continuing to improve week over week.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 5.5 percent change, it signals a threshold level of reduced home-confinement behavior, triggering a disproportionate surge in discretionary retail and recreation trips as pent-up demand is released beyond the gradual baseline trend.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.7 to 5.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses below 5.5 but RETAIL_REC does not show an accelerated rise relative to the pre-threshold trend rate over the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a compounding reopening effect: commuting enables transit use and vice versa, and together they amplify retail recovery beyond what either series predicts alone, because combined mobility restores both access and occasion for shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved concurrently across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over 28 days is no larger than the sum of the marginal effects predicted from WORKPLACES and TRANSIT individually, indicating no interaction amplification.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week volatility in PARKS (-36.0, -39.3, -35.7, -38.1) without a clear trend suggests outdoor recreation substitution is unstable and not a reliable predictor; this noise masks any genuine shift in retail behavior, meaning PARKS swings do not translate into RETAIL_REC movement at all.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change exceeds 3 points in either direction
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated between -39.3 and -35.7 without monotonic direction
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a clear directional move in the same direction as the most recent PARKS swing, indicating PARKS volatility is informative rather than noise.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility suddenly falls by more than 10 points week-on-week from its current recovering level, this would indicate a reimposition of movement restrictions, which would reverse the current gradual retail recovery and push RETAIL_REC sharply lower over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT currently improving gradually from -39.4 to -37.4
failure_condition: TRANSIT drops more than 10 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not subsequently decline over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The stable, near-flat trajectory of GROCERY_PHARM (around 1 percent change, essential-goods baseline) indicates no seasonal essential-demand shock is occurring, implying that any movement in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is driven by discretionary recovery trends rather than panic-buying or essential-goods seasonality.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within 0.4 to 1.4 percent for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains flat while RETAIL_REC moves downward over the next 28 days, contradicting the assumption that flat essential demand implies discretionary-driven retail growth.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL together signals a coordinated behavioral shift away from home-centric living toward external activity, and this joint movement predicts a stronger and faster rise in RETAIL_REC than either series would indicate alone, since commuting and reduced home-dwelling jointly free up time and occasion for retail trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -14.6 to -13.0 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.7 to 5.9 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 14 days is no greater than what WORKPLACES alone would predict, showing no additional lift from the concurrent RESIDENTIAL decline.
